title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is items 9 and 10 of section V, 'Résumons les avatars des trois groupes'. That section lists the many incarnations of the extended modular group PGL(2,Z) and its index-2 subgroup PSL(2,Z). Item 6 on the previous page, the triangulated cartographic group Γ_{∞,3}, is one of them; T'_{1,1} = T_{1,1}/{±1} is another. These groups are then used in section VI to study loop-preserving ('à lacets') automorphisms of the profinite group Π̂_{0,3}, in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller spirit.

Item 9, conformal case. M^conf_{1,1} is the modular orbifold ('multiplicité modulaire') of conformal elliptic curves, i.e. Riemann surfaces of type (1,1) up to both holomorphic and antiholomorphic isomorphisms. Its π_1 is GL(2,Z). Dividing by the centre {±1} gives PGL(2,Z). This equals π_1 of M'^conf_{1,1}, the moduli of conformal elliptic curves 'modulo symmetry', i.e. modulo the generic automorphism z↦−z. In modern terms M' is the rigidification of the stack by its generic stabiliser μ_2.

Item 9, analytic case. The holomorphic analogues are π_1(M^an_{1,1}) = SL(2,Z), with quotient by the centre ≅ PSL(2,Z) ≅ π_1(M'^an_{1,1}).

Base point. The base point is the Eisenstein curve C/(Z + Z(−j)), with j = e^{2πi/3} and −j a primitive 6th root of unity. This curve has CM by Z[j] and the maximal automorphism group μ_6. The choice matches the base point '−J' used on the previous page for U_{0,3} (à la Malgoire).

Orbifold presentations. The modular orbifolds are (D, GL(2,Z)) and (D, SL(2,Z)) for M_{1,1}, in the conformal resp. analytic setting. Here D is the upper half-plane, and det −1 elements act antiholomorphically, z ↦ (a z̄ + b)/(c z̄ + d). For M'_{1,1} they are (D, GL(2,Z)' = GP(1,Z)) resp. (D, SL(2,Z)' = GP(1,Z)^+). The notation GP(1,Z) means PGL(2,Z) and GP(1,Z)^+ means PSL(2,Z).

Item 10 records the purely group-theoretic avatar: GL(2,Z)' ≅ PGL(2,Z), with subgroup SL(2,Z)' ≅ PSL(2,Z).

Taken together, the list identifies PGL(2,Z) ≅ Γ_{∞,3} with the extended (2,3,∞) triangle group, with π_1 of the conformal moduli orbifold, and with the extended mapping class groups. The aim is to have all these incarnations available before computing Aut ext of Π̂_{0,3} and Ŝ^+_{0,3} on the next page.
errors: No mathematical errors. A minor inconsistency in the draft: line 1 is written with the superscript 'conf', while the explanatory sentence first says M^an and then corrects it to 'conf'. Grothendieck's overwriting ('analytique' → 'conformes') shows he was still settling the conformal vs analytic terminology.

ideas.what: π_1 of the moduli orbifold of elliptic curves is SL(2,Z), and is GL(2,Z) when antiholomorphic isomorphisms are allowed (conformal / 'dianalytic' moduli). Modulo the centre this gives PSL(2,Z) / PGL(2,Z), which equals π_1 of the rigidified moduli.
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group of M_{1,1}; rigidification M_{1,1} → M_{1,1}/μ_2; real/dianalytic moduli via the extended modular group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke); stack-theoretic rigidification due to Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and SL(2,Z) / the cartographic group in the same spirit; this exact list is unpublished

ideas.what: Choice of the Eisenstein curve C/(Z + Z(−j)), which has the maximal automorphism group μ_6, as the base point. This matches the base point −J on U_{0,3}.
ideas.modern_name: Tangential/orbifold base point at the CM point ρ = e^{iπ/3}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; base points at elliptic points are common in GT/Ihara-type work

ideas.what: Notation GP(1,Z) = PGL(2,Z) and GP(1,Z)^+ = PSL(2,Z) as avatars of the triangulated cartographic group Γ_{∞,3} and its oriented subgroup.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; cartographic interpretation by Grothendieck (Esquisse); Jones–Singerman
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme, §3 (cartographic groups and PSL(2,Z))

deep.surprise_reason: This is a bookkeeping page listing standard identifications: π_1 of the conformal/analytic M_{1,1} as GL(2,Z)/SL(2,Z), with quotients by the centre PGL(2,Z)/PSL(2,Z). Everything is classical. The only personal touches are the 'conformal' (antiholomorphic-allowed) framing and the Eisenstein base point, both natural and present in later literature in other forms.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the first M carries the superscript 'conf', and the right-hand side is M'^{conf}_{1,1}.
'π_1(Y)/centre{±1}' is a doubtful reading. The symbol after π_1 is unclear; it probably denotes the same group, with the centre {±1} quotiented out, and not a space Y.
'courbe {+ell. conformes resp.+} analytique': the insertion reads 'ell. conformes resp.' above 'analytique', i.e. 'la courbe ell. conforme resp. analytique'.
'337' at the top is Grothendieck's own manuscript pagination (cf. the range 293–650); '95' is the archive page number.
